slides.say: Given: p squared is smaller than p, which is smaller than r times q, which is smaller than q, which is smaller than r. Which of the following statements is possible but not necessarily true?

A long chain of letters. So before the choices, let's decode it. [short pause] Start with p squared smaller than p. Can p be negative? No. Its square would be positive, and bigger than p. So p is positive, and squaring made it smaller. That happens only to positive fractions.
p is positive, so everything bigger in the chain is positive too. Now r q is smaller than q. q is positive, so divide both sides by q, and r is smaller than one.
So all of them are positive fractions, p the smallest, and r the biggest.
Now the question. Possible but not necessarily true. So anything always true is out, and anything never true is out too.
Choice number three, p q against p plus q. Multiplying by a fraction pulls toward zero, so p q is smaller than p. Adding q makes p bigger. So the product is smaller than the sum, always. Out.
at: p q against p plus q

slides.say: Choice number one. Divide both sides by p, which is positive, and it's p q against r. p q is smaller than q, and q is smaller than r. Always true. Out. Or strong on strong. p squared against p, p wins, and q against r, r wins. The right side wins twice.
Choice number two, p q bigger than one. A product of two positive fractions is always below one. Never true. Out.
at: A product of two positive fractions

slides.say: Choice number four, p plus r smaller than one. Two fractions. Small ones add up to less than one, big ones to more. p is one tenth, q two fifths, and r one half. The chain holds, and p plus r is three fifths, smaller than one. But p one quarter, q three quarters, and r seven eighths. The chain still holds, and p plus r is nine eighths, more than one. Sometimes true, sometimes not. Choice number four is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number four is our answer
